doctrine: Threads (Meta's Twitter-alternative) operates on a conversation-graph algorithm that prioritizes replies/interactions over likes/follows. Key growth mechanics: 1) Post frequency 5-7+ times daily for algorithm visibility; 2) Profile setup: clear headshot, identity line + direction line + CTA in bio, stick to visual theme for recognition; 3) Content strategy: long-form posts with 6-8 points + hooks with numbers + natural/conversational tone; 4) Algorithm prioritizes meaningful social interaction (MSI) and conversation-driven engagement; 5) Text-only posts outperform image/video posts; 6) Repurposing Twitter/LinkedIn content does NOT work; 7) Community engagement matters more than reach: reply to 5-10 big accounts daily, quote posts, jump into random conversations; 8) Posting frequency creates sample size for A/B learning; 9) Short content shelf life requires daily+ posting vs once/week; 10) Visual content (photos/videos) gets significant promotion; 11) Hashtags/current tactics not yet established; 12) Instant community from Instagram follow-all feature; 13) ~400M+ active users (per Meta); 14) Local/regional posts perform exceptionally well (e.g., 'who in LA wants podcast'); 15) Rage-baiting works but risks brand damage; 16) Schedule content 2-5x per week minimum; 17) 500 character limit per post (vs Twitter's 240); 18) Private account deletion requires Instagram account deletion; 19) EU access restricted due to privacy regulations.

contradictions: Visual content (photos/videos) promoted significantly according to some creators, yet text-only posts outperform images/videos according to Sendible data. Likely platform evolution or niche-dependent.

Repurposing content fails universally stated, yet multiple sources recommend cross-posting from Twitter/LinkedIn via automation tools like HypeFury. Likely means copy-paste fails, but native adaptation works.
Some sources claim 10+ posts/day needed, others claim 2-5/week minimum. Likely early-adopter advantage peaked; consistency matters more than volume now.
Algorithm described as 'light' (chronological-heavy) yet also conversation-graph driven with recommendation engine. Both true: light compared to Instagram's heavy algorithmic feed.
